subject: wildlife-animals
label: Wildlife Lab — fox, rabbit, and glowcap tortoise
notes: RAHEEM APPROVED a 200-generation hard ceiling on 2026-08-07 for three eight-direction animal bases and the animation needed to make every initial behavior visually honest.
ANIMALS ONLY. No trees, ponds, dens, plants, scenery, ground patches, cast shadows, or habitat props are part of this batch.
The animals are built in a separate WildlifeLab scene. CourtyardV2.scene is not modified or used as the generation surface.
The low top-down view matches the locked courtyard camera language: body and face cues remain readable while feet stay anchored to the ground.

LIVE API CORRECTION, 2026-08-07: /create-8-direction-object rejects both seed and style_images when creating directly from a description. The first request 422ed before generation and cost 0. These animals are therefore not seed-reproducible; preserve the raw provider job, object id, all eight rotations, exact prompt, actual usage, validation result, runtime review, and human approval state.

After the base pass, object ids are copied into the animation config. Movement and every initial signature activity are animated in down, left, right, and up facings so an activity never snaps the animal to an unrelated direction.
No blind rerolls. Retry only an objectively broken or zero-usage stalled job while the full batch remains under 200 generations.

FISH, 2026-08-10. The 200-generation ceiling above covered the first three animals and is closed at 196; Raheem opened a new budget for water life. Full four directions approved, one ordinary pond fish.

GENERATION SIZE IS NOT WORLD SIZE, and the fish is where that first bites. The animals are generated at 168 and drawn at 0.4-0.7 scale, a mild downscale. A fish reads at roughly 35px in a 364px pond, so generating it at 168 would mean a 0.2 downscale and the pixel grid would be destroyed - the same defect measured on the Leonardo pond before it was redrawn. Generated at 64 so its native pixels are close to the size they are shown at.
